match.reason: No point in the bank covers e-marketing; the closest, market research for a new business, is about learning about customers before starting, not marketing through digital channels.

draft.title: E-marketing
card: E-marketing is marketing done online. It uses websites, social media, email and search engines to reach customers and promote products.
It can target customers closely. A business can choose who sees an ad by age, location or interests, and can email people who have already shown interest.
It can measure results quickly. A business can see clicks, visits, sales and sign-ups within hours or days, and use them to adjust a campaign.
Search marketing places a business in front of people who are already searching for a product, such as a link shown above search results.
draft.remember: E-marketing reaches chosen customers online and shows the results fast.

a.q: Why can a business adjust an e-marketing campaign sooner than a printed brochure drop?
opts: It can see clicks and sales data within hours or days
It can reach every customer in the country at once
It no longer needs to choose a target market
It can avoid paying for any advertising space
a.why: Online tools report clicks, visits and sales quickly, so a business can change the campaign while it runs. Reaching everyone is not what the card says: e-marketing aims to target chosen customers, not all of them.
a.clue: Think about what the business can see soon after the campaign starts.

b.q: Priya sells hiking boots from her Hobart website. She shows ads only to people in Tasmania who follow outdoor pages. Which feature of e-marketing is she using?
opts: Close targeting of customers
Quick measurement of results
Search engine placement
Email contact with past buyers
b.why: Priya chooses who sees the ad by location and interests, which is close targeting. Measurement would involve checking clicks or sales after the ads run, which she has not done in this case.
b.clue: Look at how she chooses who sees the ads.

a.best: It can see clicks and sales data within hours or days

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a precise detail ('within hours or days'), copied from the card. The three distractors all use sweeping absolutes ('no longer', 'every customer', 'any advertising space'). A student could pick the answer by elimination without knowing the idea.

a.q: Why can a business adjust an e-marketing campaign sooner than a printed brochure drop?
opts: It gets data on clicks and sales soon after ads go live
It shows its ads to people grouped by age and interests
It reaches people who are already searching for it
It sends emails to people who have shown interest
a.why: Online tools report clicks, visits and sales quickly, so the business can see how the campaign is going and change it while it runs. Choosing people by age and interests is targeting: it decides who sees the ad, but it does not tell the business whether the ad is working.
a.clue: To change a campaign, what does a business first need to know?
